# rowstile

> Authorization for apps on Postgres: sharing, groups, nested folders and tenants, with no service beside the
> database. A policy file (`.authz`) says who can do what; the `rowstile` command compiles it
> into row-level security, trigger-maintained tables for inheritance and `authz.*` SQL functions, and ships
> each change as a migration for the app's own tool (Alembic, Prisma, Drizzle Kit, SQL, goose, dbmate,
> Flyway). Any Postgres 16, 17 or 18; no extension, no superuser. SDKs for Python (FastAPI, SQLAlchemy) and
> TypeScript (Next.js, Prisma, Drizzle, pg, postgres.js, React).

What an agent needs to know:

- The policy lives in one file named by `rowstile.toml` (`policy = "db/policy.authz"`), with tests beside it
  (`tests = ["db/tests/*.authz"]`). Everything that grants access is written in the policy.
- The loop after editing it: `rowstile check` (the first mistake, with its line and a code like `[AZ201]`),
  `rowstile push` (the development database only), `rowstile test`. Or `rowstile dev`, which does all three on
  each save. `rowstile help AZ201` explains a code and shows the mistake fixed.
- Production takes migrations: `rowstile migrate` writes the next one from `db/policy.lock`; never `push`.
- App code checks nothing by hand. Each transaction signs in (`SELECT authz.act_as('user', '42')`, which the
  SDKs do), then plain queries are filtered, refused writes raise SQLSTATE 42501 with the reason (the SDKs
  answer 403), and rows the user can't see are 404.
- `rowstile mcp` is an MCP server with the command's tools: `check`, `prove`, `review`, `test`, `why`, `lint`
  and `push`.

When it fits, and when it doesn't:

- It fits an app whose data is in one Postgres database, where who may see or change a row depends on other
  rows: its owner, the members of a team (teams inside teams), a folder or a project that passes access down,
  a tenant, what people share with each other.
- The policy reads the tables the app already has. There is no second store to write to and keep in step, a
  list of what someone may see is an ordinary query (joined, sorted, paged), and a share commits with the row
  it is about.
- It doesn't fit when what decides access is in several databases, or outside Postgres; when a browser reads
  the tables through Supabase's Data API (its roles are not the app role: a backend has to sign in); or when
  one type takes many structural writes a second (moves and links in a tree wait for each other).
- It is a 0.x preview, and nobody outside the project has audited it: say so when you suggest it.

A small policy:

```authz
app role app_user                               -- the Postgres role the app connects as
type user = app.users
type folder = app.folders
  owner  : user   = owner_id                    -- a relation read from a column
  parent : folder = parent_id
  editor : user   = app.folder_editors(folder_id -> user_id)   -- ... or from a link table
  can edit = owner or editor or parent.edit     -- inherited down the tree
  can view = edit
rules app.folders
  select : view
  update : edit
```

## Docs

- [The policy language](docs/reference/language.md): types, relations, permissions, inheritance, denies, rules, masks, invariants, tests
- [Using it from app code](docs/reference/app-code.md): every `authz.*` function, the generated clients, refusals that say why
- [Identity](docs/reference/identity.md): a trusted backend, API keys and scopes, JWTs, services; signed sessions
- [Governance](docs/reference/governance.md): audit trail, change feed, requests, break glass, reviews; `authz.lint()`
- [Tools](docs/reference/tools.md): every `rowstile` command, `rowstile.toml`, the MCP server
- [Migrations](docs/reference/migrations.md): a policy change as a migration for your tool, the lock file
- [Reviewing a change](docs/reference/review.md): what `rowstile review` says on a pull request
- [How it works](docs/reference/guarantees.md): what it compiles to, what it guarantees, security
- [Speed and limits](docs/reference/limits.md): measured speed, and what it doesn't do
- [Installing](docs/installing.md): npm, pip or the image; alphas, betas and release candidates; from the repository
- [rowstile and the alternatives](docs/comparison.md): authorization services, policy engines, rules in the ORM, row-level security by hand; when each is the better choice
- [How rowstile is checked](docs/how-it-is-checked.md): what tests it, and what has not been done (no outside audit)
- [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md): from a schema to a policy, tests, the dev loop and migrations (run as written by the tests)
- [Cookbook](docs/cookbook.md): nineteen tested recipes, a page each (tenants, roles, teams inside teams, folders that inherit, sharing and links, requests, masks, soft deletes, bots, API keys with scopes, blocking, live updates)
- [Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md): what people run into, by what they see
- [Running rowstile](docs/operations.md): configuration, behind a pooler, deploying a change, upgrading, backups, retention, what to watch
- [Managed Postgres](docs/managed-postgres.md): the setup on a managed service; Neon and Supabase, as tried
- [Files in S3-compatible storage](docs/signed-urls.md): signed URLs handed out only after the row was read
- [Error codes](docs/errors/README.md): every mistake's code, what it means and the same mistake fixed
- [Playground](playground/README.md): the compiler and Postgres in the browser, nothing installed

## Stacks

- [Stacks](docs/stacks/README.md): pick yours
- [FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, Alembic](docs/stacks/fastapi.md): the Python SDK with FastAPI
- [Next.js, Prisma, React](docs/stacks/nextjs.md): the TypeScript SDK with Next.js
- [Node: pg, postgres.js, Drizzle](docs/stacks/node.md): any Node app
- [Python: SQLAlchemy, SQLModel, psycopg, asyncpg](docs/stacks/python.md): any Python app
- [Any other stack](docs/stacks/sql.md): the SQL an app sends
- [Python SDK](sdk/python/README.md): `pip install --pre rowstile` (an alpha so far), its modules
- [TypeScript SDK](sdk/typescript/README.md): the `@rowstile/*` packages
